subject.title: fix: require decimal numeric oc-path predicates

question: Should relational oc-path predicates continue accepting all finite JavaScript numeric spellings, or should OpenClaw intentionally narrow the public grammar to plain decimal literals?
rationale: The patch changes previously accepted predicate input rather than fixing an unambiguous parser defect, and repository policy treats compatibility-sensitive behavior changes as requiring maintainer-visible direction.

options.title: Preserve finite-number compatibility
options.body: Keep finite exponent and hexadecimal forms working, then narrowly address any undesired blank-string or coercion case without narrowing the established predicate grammar.

options.title: Adopt decimal-only predicates
options.body: Approve the compatibility break, document the decimal-only grammar and upgrade impact, and require tests proving the intended rejection and supported migration story.

recommendation.title: Preserve finite-number compatibility
recommendation.body: Keep finite exponent and hexadecimal forms working, then narrowly address any undesired blank-string or coercion case without narrowing the established predicate grammar.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only explicitly identified human participant in the supplied PR timeline who can route the unresolved behavior-contract choice.
